text.p: Italian food group Parmalat Finanziaria said stock market talk of a possible capital operation and rumours about its results were "unfounded".
"The rumours circulating on the market relating to capital operations and talk about 1996 results are absolutely unfounded," a spokesman for Parmalat said.

Earlier Parmalat shares were losing around seven percent on the Milan bourse, with dealers reporting rumours the company might issue a convertible bond and that its 1996 results were going to be poorer than expected.
Ordinary shares, which dipped to 2490 lire during the session, climbed back to stand 4.83 percent down on the day at 2560, against an overall market which was around half a percentage point down.
Volume on the dairy produce group's shares was 17.5 million shares by 1555 GMT.
